source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: Truth Values of Propositions with a small program of ours that counts the 2^n rows (PDF 29, printed 25).

blocks.text: Har proposition, jaise P ya Q, ki value True (T) ya False (F) ho sakti hai. Truth table tamam mumkin combinations likhta hai: n propositions ke liye 2ⁿ rows. Maslan 2 propositions ke liye 2² = 4 rows aur 3 ke liye 2³ = 8 rows. Compound proposition ki truth value us ke hisson (components) ki values se tay hoti hai.
n propositions ke liye 2ⁿ rows kyun? Yeh program saari rows gin kar aur likh kar dikhata hai. n badal kar Run karein.

from itertools import product

n = 3   # propositions ki tadaad (P, Q, R)

rows = list(product([True, False], repeat=n))
print("Propositions:", n)
print("Rows:", len(rows), "= 2 ki power", n)
for row in rows:
    print(" ".join("T" if v else "F" for v in row))

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"from itertools import product": Python ki standard library se product function, jo saare combinations bana deta hai.
"n = 3": teen propositions (maslan P, Q, R).
"product([True, False], repeat=n)": True/False ke saare mumkin jor (combinations) banata hai; list() se un ki list ban jati hai.
len(rows): rows ki tadaad; n = 3 ke liye 2 x 2 x 2 = 8.
Aakhri loop har row ko T aur F mein likhta hai ("T" if v else "F").
Output: "Propositions: 3", "Rows: 8 = 2 ki power 3", phir 8 rows: T T T, T T F, T F T, T F F, F T T, F T F, F F T, F F F.
Khud try karein: n = 2 kar ke Run karein: "Rows: 4" aur chaar rows (T T, T F, F T, F F). n = 4 par 16 rows aayengi.

items: Har proposition T ya F hota hai.
n propositions ke liye 2ⁿ rows (2 ke liye 4, 3 ke liye 8).
Compound proposition ki value us ke hisson ki values se tay hoti hai.
